sentences.ko: 내일 뉴욕 가. 가는 건 진짜 싫은데, 그래도 아들 볼 수 있으니까.
sentences.text: I'm leaving for New York tomorrow, which I hate, but I get to see my son, who I love.

alts.text: Off to New York tomorrow. Hate the trip, but I get to see my son.
Tomorrow I depart for New York, which I do not enjoy, but I will be able to see my son.

sentences.note: **get to** 는 "~할 수 있게 되다"로, 하고 싶던 일이 기회로 주어질 때 씁니다. 싫은 것과 좋은 것을 한 문장에 붙일 때 **which I hate** 처럼 앞 내용을 통째로 받아 덧붙이면 말맛이 삽니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 1 | Friends

sentences.ko: 여기 오는 길에 사람들이 다 쳐다보더라.
sentences.text: I turned quite a few heads on my way over here.

alts.text: Everybody was staring at me walking over.
Quite a few people turned to look at me as I made my way here.

sentences.note: **turned quite a few heads** 는 차림새나 모습이 눈에 띄어 사람들이 돌아봤다는 뜻으로, 으쓱할 때 농담처럼 씁니다. **on my way over here** 는 "여기 오는 길에".
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 10 | Friends

sentences.ko: 너네 그 카페에서 너무 죽치고 있는 거 아니야?
sentences.text: You guys hang out at the coffee house way too much.

alts.text: Honestly, you two basically live at that coffee place.
All of you spend far too much time at that coffee house.

sentences.note: **hang out** 은 특별한 일 없이 어울려 시간을 보내는 것. **way too much** 는 way 가 too 를 한 번 더 밀어 주는 강조로, 친한 사이에 가볍게 타박할 때 씁니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 5 | Friends

sentences.ko: 우리도 입양 준비할 때 똑같은 일 겪었어.
sentences.text: We went through the same thing when we were adopting.

alts.text: Same thing happened to us back when we were adopting.
Our family experienced the very same thing while we were adopting.

sentences.note: **went through** 는 힘든 일을 겪어 지나왔다는 뜻이라, 지금 고생하는 사람에게 "나도 그랬다"고 할 때 딱 맞습니다. **the same thing** 을 붙여 통째로 씁니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones That Make You Laugh: Part 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 내가 만나 본 남자들은 대부분 자기 얘기만 계속해.
sentences.text: Most guys I go out with, they just talk and talk.

alts.text: Almost every guy I date just talks nonstop.
The majority of the men I have dated do nothing but talk.

sentences.note: **go out with** 는 사귀거나 데이트한다는 뜻입니다. **talk and talk** 처럼 같은 동사를 and 로 이어 붙이면 "끝도 없이 계속한다"는 지겨움이 묻어납니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones That Make You Laugh: Part 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 나도 어쩔 수 없었어. 그렇게 할 수밖에 없었다고.
sentences.text: I mean, I I did what I had to do.

alts.text: Look, I just did what I had to do.
Ultimately, I did what I had to do.

sentences.note: **did what I had to do** 는 마음이 편치는 않지만 달리 방법이 없어서 그렇게 했다고 자기 입장을 밝힐 때 씁니다. 잘했다는 자랑이 아니라 '나도 선택지가 없었다'에 가깝습니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 5 | Friends

sentences.text: This was supposed to be a temp job.

alts.text: It was only supposed to be temporary.
Originally, the position was supposed to be temporary.

sentences.note: **supposed to be** 는 원래 계획은 그랬는데 지금은 아니라는 아쉬움을 담아 말할 때 씁니다. 임시로 하는 일은 **a temp job** 이라고 부릅니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 1 | Friends

sentences.ko: 하필 내가 면접 보던 그 식당에 우리 팀장이 있었어. 얘기를 다 들었더라고.
sentences.text: Well, my boss was at the same restaurant where I was having my interview and he heard everything.

alts.text: Turns out my boss happened to be at the same restaurant during my interview, and he heard everything.
Unfortunately, my supervisor was at the restaurant where my interview took place, and he overheard the entire conversation.

sentences.note: **heard everything** 은 '숨기려던 걸 상대가 다 들어 버렸다'는 뜻으로 들킨 상황에 씁니다. 하필 그 자리에 있었다는 우연은 **happened to be** 로 말합니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 10 | Friends

sentences.ko: 그 얘기는 너희 중에 누가 결혼하면 그때 하자.
sentences.text: How about we have this conversation when one of you guys gets married?

alts.text: Let's save this talk for when one of you actually gets married.
Perhaps we could postpone this discussion until one of you is married.

sentences.note: **How about we** 뒤에 동사를 그대로 붙이면 '우리 ~하는 거 어때?' 하고 가볍게 제안하는 말이 됩니다. 지금은 말고 나중에 하자고 미룰 때는 **save this talk for** 를 씁니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 5 | Friends

sentences.ko: 여기 벽이 얇아서 옆집 소리가 다 들려.
sentences.text: Yeah, you can hear everything through these stupid walls.

alts.text: Honestly, the walls here are so thin you hear it all.
The walls in this building are so thin that every sound carries.

sentences.note: 방음이 안 되는 집을 말할 때 **you can hear everything** 을 그대로 씁니다. 벽 자체를 말할 때는 **so thin** 처럼 두께로 표현합니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 10 | Friends
